title: Projects
text:
Here are some data science and statistics-related projects I have worked on.



Fall 2025 - Spring 2026
I worked with Yvonne Yang, MD, PhD and Thomas Maierhofer, PhD as a statistician to help analyze data from clinical study of healthy patients, clinical high risk, and schizophrenic patients. Participants had their brain inflammation measured using [18F]FEPPA as a PET radiotracer and took the Traumatic Experience Checklist survey (Nijenhuis et al., 2016) which was the primary indicator of interest. Responsibilities involved model fitting, hypothesis testing, exploring potential sub-analyses, as well as various data-related tasks (cleaning, transformation, sample testing). Ultimately, I fit multiple fixed linear models and a mixed effects model accounting for repeated measures and covariate effects. These ended up showing no significant relationship between trauma experience and brain inflammation. I presented these results at the UCLA Undergraduate Research Week in May 2026.
Link to recorded presentation
Link to slide deck



Winter 2026
Analyzed psychometric assessment profiles for over 60,000 global senior business leaders to evaluate drivers of emotional and cognitive capacity. Executed two-way ANOVA, MANOVA, Welch t-tests, and OLS linear regressions in R to isolate structural determinants of leadership traits. Quantified practical effect sizes (partial \(\eta^2\) and \(R^2\)) to show that country of upbringing explains 10% of cognitive adaptability variance, while management tenure accounts for less than 1%. Presented findings to a panel of industry experts, highlighting actionable insights for targeted marketing strategies.
Link to report



Fall 2025
Cleaned and aggregated a heterogeneous dataset of user purchase histories from 5,000+ individuals, utilizing regular expressions to cluster 1,800+ product categories into 19 umbrella metrics. Engineered user-level behavioral features, including average spending trends, order frequencies, and geographical location matrices. Tuned and evaluated Random Forest and XGBoost regression models using 5-fold cross-validation and random/grid search with the goal of predicting consumers’ household size.
Link to report



Winter 2025
Analyzed 150K+ U.S. commercial real estate leases and federal unemployment data from metro-areas in a team of 5. Developed a rent resilience index to quantify market resilience to economic stressors like vacancy and unemployment. Presented findings to professional data scientists and industry leaders; selected as one of 15 finalists out of 80+ teams in DataFest 2025.
Link to slide deck

title: Charlie Kopp
text:
Hello! My name’s Charlie Kopp. I am a proud nerd with a passion for mental health advocacy and highlighting the unique connections that bring humans together in mind and spirit.
I am currently studying Statistics and Data Science at UCLA, but what makes me special is my personal journey through sobriety and recovery, and experience with interpersonal communication and leadership.
I have battled through addiction and mental health crises, granting me a newfound appreciation for life after becoming sober at 19. Throughout my life I have witnessed the prevalence of technology used to drive outrage, encourage isolation, and destroy community. However, I firmly believe there exists another path where data and technology can be used to better humanity and bring us together.
Using kindness, transparency and dedication I believe we can make this planet a place where everyone can live with dignity, comfort and joy.
